extracted.intended_audience: aspiring journalists, newspaper editors, and personal/staff secretaries to prominent figures
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practical criteria for running a newspaper and for the conduct, selection, and duties of personal secretaries on a newspaper proprietor's staff, drawn from narrated practice and a proprietor's lecture. Covers editorial/newsroom values, stylistic qualities, commercial considerations, and detailed expectations for secretarial performance and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy (news accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy, accuracy, accuracy -- make every one connected with the paper believe that accuracy is to a newspaper what virtue is to a woman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take extraordinary pains to be accurate: editors, reporters, correspondents, rewrite men, proof-readers must all be made to value accuracy. Not enough merely to avoid deliberate fake news; constant watchfulness, checking, and comparison of versions are required. The proprietor's letters, cables, and daily instructions should emphasize accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid publishing fake news
rubrics_metrics.description: Refrain from publishing what you know to be false or from tampering with the news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If staff suppress or falsify news (for example, to please an advertiser) they should be dismissed. The paper must not habitually publish fake news; exceptional care and checks should prevent knowingly false reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance sensationalism with decency
rubrics_metrics.description: A newspaper should be scrupulously accurate and clean, avoiding everything salacious or suggestive that could offend good taste or lower moral tone, but within those limits it has a duty to print news including dramatic accounts of crimes and scandals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print long and dramatic accounts of murders, wrecks, fires, lynchings, corruption, embezzlement, frauds, divorces, etc., when they are newsworthy, but link frankness with decency. Good taste means frankness braced by decency, not suppression of unpleasant facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of publicity as a reform tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity is the essential means by which a democracy exposes secret vices and sweeps them away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose crimes, dodges, tricks, and swindles in the press so public opinion can act. Publicity may not be sufficient alone, but without it other agencies will fail; this justifies thorough reporting of wrongdoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circulation and financial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A newspaper must aim for big circulation because reach and advertising revenue give independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large circulation ensures news and comment reach many people; advertising brings money, and money buys independence. Never suppress news to placate advertisers; editorial independence depends on financial strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial honesty with editorial discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: An editorial may strongly support particular views while printing the truth and nothing but the truth, but the editor may exercise discretion about printing the whole truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial pages need not form public opinion single-handedly; readers form opinions from a mix of facts and near-facts. Editors should state views forcefully but avoid gratuitous disclosures that serve no public purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: News and editorial stylistic qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: News, headlines, and editorials require terseness, humor, descriptive power, satire, originality, good literary style, clever condensation, and accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These qualities should guide headlines, the editorial page, and the writing throughout the paper to make content engaging and effective for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for personal staff/secretaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of personal staff must consider usefulness to the employer, trustworthiness in confidential relationships, and social fitness to associate with the employer's family (including ladies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise extreme caution in making selections; obtain references from people and households where the candidate has been a guest, and investigate character and social suitability before appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretarial knowledge and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretaries must be thoroughly prepared: know facts, figures, plays, and subjects in depth; be ready to be cross-examined and to supply accurate information on demand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proprietor tests staff by abrupt questioning (e.g., 'begin at the second scene of the third act'). A secretary must memorize, verify numbers, read and check articles on request, and be able to carry topics forward from any point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memory and attention to detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to memorize and precisely recall figures, program details, local observations, and other small facts is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to recite committed figures from memory, have clippings and references available, and assist by checking figures against articles; routine checking by colleagues may reveal mistakes immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion and calm under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain perfect calmness and self-possession; avoid showing nervousness, excitement, or engaging in public altercations that would upset the employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When walking, dining, or in public, speak in a steady tone, conceal anxiety, defuse intrusions without argument, and prevent events that would cause days of misery to the employer. Physical protection must be combined with emotional restraint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability, endurance, and adaptability
rubrics_metrics.description: Staff must be available at short notice, accept long and unpredictable working hours, and adapt to sudden schedule changes (e.g., sudden yacht departures or cancellations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to pack and embark immediately, work from early morning until late at night (reported 8 a.m. to 10–11 p.m.), and cope with repeated last-minute changes of plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observational reporting for vicarious description
rubrics_metrics.description: When providing material for someone who cannot see, record minute, concrete details (counts, steps, numbers, precise descriptions) so the principal can absorb 'material' vicariously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count fish spots, steps, people in a room, vessels in sight, etc.; carry a notebook and pencil to seize epigrams or incidents and dedicate them to the next day's duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Music knowledge and critical listening
rubrics_metrics.description: A knowledgeable musical taste and memory are valuable: able to read the program, remember performances, and criticize playing from musical experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend concerts with the employer, read programs aloud, identify when a movement is too loud or too fast, recall past performances for comparison, and convey musical impressions accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical comfort and environment control
rubrics_metrics.description: Control of sensory environment: avoid cigarette smoke, offensive odors, paints or noises when the employer is aboard or present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not smoke near the employer; prevent painting or noisy work when aboard; be mindful of scents and sounds that distress the blind employer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversational skill: entertain and inform
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversation should combine entertainment and information: be prepared with bright, satirical, or witty material and a 'solid body of carefully prepared facts' to sustain walks and social occasions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be ready to recite epigrams, character sketches, or topical material; know when to expose ignorance or reveal useful talent; keep conversation light when requested and more serious when appropriate.
